subject: vanishing glacier river
title: What If a River Vanished in Four Days? One Did in 2016, and Didn't Come Back

scenes.text: What if a whole river disappeared in four days? In 2016, one did, and it hasn't come back.
The Slims River in Canada's Yukon ran from the Kaskawulsh Glacier north to Kluane Lake and on toward the Bering Sea.
Over the last century, the glacier pulled back about a mile. In spring 2016, meltwater carved a canyon 30 metres deep through its toe.
Between May 26 and 29, the gauges dropped. The water had found a new exit, into another river, heading for the Pacific instead.
By summer, Kluane Lake was a metre lower than ever recorded, its exposed bed throwing up dust storms. The Slims was a long, skinny puddle.
Geologists call it river piracy. Nobody had seen it happen in modern times. One glacier moved, and a river changed oceans.

description:
What if a river simply vanished? Between 26 and 29 May 2016 the Slims River in Canada's Yukon did: meltwater from the retreating Kaskawulsh Glacier cut a 30 metre canyon through the ice and diverted the flow into the Kaskawulsh River, toward the Gulf of Alaska instead of the Bering Sea.
Kluane Lake fell about a metre below any recorded level and its dry bed began producing dust storms. The study in Nature Geoscience called it the first case of river piracy observed in modern times, with a 99.5 percent probability that the glacier's retreat reflects modern climate change.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The lake the river used to feed may end up with no outlet at all, turning salty over centuries. Which disappearing act should we run through next?
